basis: Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses, with widespread bone and joint abnormalities.
Cranioacral skeletal and hand abnormalities with congenital septal and pulmonary-valve defects; limited syndrome data.
Low-grade neuroendocrine tumor arising in rectal mucosa; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Dyskeratosis congenita features marrow failure, nail/skin abnormalities and oral leukoplakia; pulmonary fibrosis is not established at >=30% for this subtype.
Defining cataracts, progressive sensorineural deafness and neurologic disease including ataxia, intellectual disability and peripheral neuropathy.
Clonal dendritic-cell neoplasm; single-system multifocal disease usually involves multiple destructive bone lesions, exceeding the 30% threshold.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Inherited aortic and arterial disease; stroke occurs in 15%, below the threshold for neurologic involvement.
Focal developmental malformation of the cerebral cortex.
Traumatic injury of the optic nerve causing visual loss; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Inherited cerebral small-vessel angiopathy defined by vascular pathology and cerebral white-matter injury.
Neurodevelopmental disease; VSD 60%, polydactyly 40% and vertebral defects 30%, hypodontia 30%. Hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.
Factor VIII deficiency; recurrent joint hemorrhage affects ~64% and causes joint damage. Oral bleeding alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Syndrome defined by infantile nephrotic kidney disease and associated ocular abnormalities.
Cerebellar degeneration with ataxia and dysarthria; laryngeal dystonia and abnormal saccades are neurologic manifestations.
Defining lip pits and cleft lip/palate involve oral structures; no separate skin or skeletal damage is established.
Complete gonadal dysgenesis with elevated FSH establishes impaired gonadal endocrine function; reproductive anatomy alone would have no axis.
Progressive astroglial leukodystrophy damages brain white matter; scoliosis is secondary to neurologic impairment rather than direct skeletal disease.
Core tumor sites span oral cavity/esophagus and pharynx/larynx/nose. Endocrine and skin tumors are optional sites in the broad definition.
Congenital cardiac valve and associated structural heart defects; urinary abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Statin toxicity predominantly causes toxic myopathy or rhabdomyolysis; hepatic injury and secondary kidney injury are not established in >=30%.
Carcinoma arises in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; misleading skin terminology and ancestry do not change its origin.
Umbrella skeletal disorder of abnormal bone mineralization; endocrine or electrolyte abnormalities depend on the subtype.
Defining spastic ataxia and corneal/cataract disease; reduced immunoglobulins are frequent (30-79%), supporting associated immune deficiency.
Restrictive skin disease; bone defects and ankylosis occur in ~100% of reported patients; pulmonary hypoplasia is common and causes neonatal respiratory failure.
